_doc: Editing grammar: which moment in the spoken text gets which effect. Single source of truth (beats.py detects moments, build_edl.py + beatfx.py apply effects, music/make_beds.py places beat SFX, critic.py checks). Edit freely; cues are Python regexes, case-insensitive, matched per sentence. Evidence and thresholds (SRC/HEUR/PROP): RESEARCH.md. sfx: null | pop | whoosh | ding (played at the beat; a punch without sfx is silent).

detect._doc: beats.py detection: up to per_sentence moments per sentence, at least min_dist words apart (one per phrase); a run of max_sentence words without . ? ! is split at the next comma; the hook (first sentence) lands on the first content word between hook_earliest and hook_latest s (shorts: visual change inside 1.5 s, RESEARCH); auto graphics keep gfx_min_gap s from other graphics; number cards drop filler words before the caption and mark approximations (około 60 -> ~60)

hook.label: Hak
hook.intent: first sentence: promise or tension that keeps the viewer

stat.label: Liczba
stat.intent: hard data: number, percent, money, time

contrast.label: Zwrot
contrast.intent: turn against expectation; the viewer's assumption flips
cues: \b(a jednak|tylko że|wbrew \w+|a mimo to|nie dlatego|a żadn\w*|problem w tym|paradoks\w*)\b

maxim.label: Puenta
maxim.intent: the line worth quoting; conclusion of a thought
cues: \b(puent\w*|(to )?(wcale )?nie znaczy|nie chodzi o|chodzi o to|klucz\w* (jest|to)|najważniejsz\w*|prawda jest taka|sedno|liczy się|nie ma znaczenia)\b

confession.label: Wyznanie
confession.intent: personal admission; builds trust, wants intimacy not hype

question.label: Pytanie
question.intent: rhetorical question; opens a loop the next sentence closes

advice.label: Rada
advice.intent: direct instruction the viewer can act on

demo.label: Pokaz
demo.intent: describes something visible (app, screen, result); show it instead of talking about it

story.label: Historia
story.intent: anecdote starts; the viewer leans in

example.label: Przykład
example.intent: concrete example makes the abstract point tangible

relatable.label: Swojskie
relatable.intent: shared experience; nod with the viewer

hook.why: one strong word of the promise gets the first punch; payoff before context (RESEARCH: hook)

list.why: structure is shown, not zoomed: animated list with pops per item

stat.why: number shown literally = proof; ding marks weight; punch only when no box (RESEARCH: stat)

contrast.why: the thought turns: short motivated punch on the turn word, silent (RESEARCH: contrast)

maxim.why: the most important line: strongest punch; max one kw quote per film (RESEARCH: maxim)

confession.why: emotion > everything: no effect, the face carries it (Murch Rule of Six; RESEARCH anti-pattern 4)

question.why: opens a loop; keep the pause after it (RESEARCH: question)

advice.why: actionable: verb in a keyword box, demo beats description (RESEARCH: advice)

story.why: anecdote stays on the speaker; optional b-roll of the place (RESEARCH: story)

relatable.why: connection moment, not a graphic moment (RESEARCH: relatable)

demo.why: what is described is shown: slide/screen with the speaker in PiP

example.why: light punch on the concrete case

pace.why: rhythm only: long stretch with no moment; consider cutting it

hook.why: visual change inside 1.5 s, hook text 5-8 words, whoosh at the start (RESEARCH: hook short)

list.why: count on screen; one icon per item

stat.why: number as big text >= 1.5 s + ding; the data point is the b-roll

maxim.why: punch 20-25% on the line to screenshot

confession.why: no effect on a confession: face + captions

question.why: question opens the loop; short pause before the answer

advice.why: verb in a keyword box, demo screen 2-3 s

section.why: no chapter cards in a short; a punch marks the step

story.why: one key image/screen of the story 1-2 s, rest on the face

cta.why: shorts: CTA in the caption/pinned comment, not on screen

demo.why: show the screen/app while it is described

pace.why: rhythm only: no moment for too long; consider cutting

long._doc: primary beats get their punch unless another punch is closer than min_gap s (RESEARCH PROP: 2-3 punches/min long, >= 10 s apart; short: 1 per 5-6 s, >= 4 s); secondary beats only when nothing happened for fill_after s; a stretch still without a visual event for max_static s (critic C1 limit) gets the 'pace' effect on the clause start nearest its middle

rules.cut_zoom: zoom level toggles on a jump cut to hide it (long: only cuts that remove >0.8 s; short: zoom_every_cut). It is a continuity device, not an emphasis effect.
rules.sfx: with beats, punches are silent unless their beat has sfx (no whoosh on every punch: SFX fatigue, RESEARCH anti-pattern 3); graphics keep their own sounds (kw/lower pop, list whoosh+pops, chap/slide whoosh, cta ding)

auto_gfx._doc: beats.py --gfx creates these graphics from moments (text = the spoken words, so the card adds no new claim; spec quote:true). long: none, its graphics are designed by hand; the rest stay suggestions (critic C10).

icons._doc: first regex (sentence text, case-insensitive) that matches picks the lucide icon of an automatic card

broll._doc: b-roll from free stock video (broll.py + stock.py): a concrete thing said in the kept text (topics: regex on ONE lowercased word, first match wins, so put specific stems first) gets dur s of matching footage from that word on. Only formats listed here (long has none: its b-roll is shot by hand). Never in a sentence holding a moment from avoid (the face carries it: RESEARCH rules 1, 10), never under a graphic, not before not_before s (hook title), min_gap s apart, at most max_share of the film, at most per_topic per query. Evidence: RESEARCH.md rule 9 (literal illustration), S12 (~35-50% coverage helps, >60-70% hurts), shorts shots <5 s.
